title: the documented session gate does not exist, and in-session releases a lock nobody holds
body:
# 0004: the documented session gate does not exist, and in-session releases a lock nobody holds

## Tags

tooling, hooks, documented-but-absent, false-green, intent-upstream

## Summary

`AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md` both state that `.claude/settings.json` wires three Claude Code lifecycle hooks -- `SessionStart`, a strict `UserPromptSubmit` gate that blocks the first prompt until `/in-session` runs, and `Stop`. None of the three exists, in this project or globally. `.claude/` contains one file, `restart.md`.

The half that DOES run makes it harder to notice. `/in-session` executes `release-gate.sh`, which writes a per-session sentinel to `/tmp/intent/`, and reports success. Nothing reads it. The release half of a mutual-exclusion mechanism runs on every session; the enforcing half was never installed.

Carried in `intent/wip.md` and the whiteboard as a prose note across two sessions. Raised as an issue because a note in a snapshot is where this goes to be forgotten, and because part of the fix is not in this repository.

## Reproduction

```
$ ls .claude/
restart.md

$ jq -r '.hooks | keys[]?' ~/.claude/settings.json
PreToolUse

$ find ~/.claude -name "require-in-session.sh"
(nothing)
```

The sentinels are real and accumulating:

```
$ ls /tmp/intent/*.sentinel | head -3
/tmp/intent/in-session-101f83f6-....sentinel
/tmp/intent/in-session-236ec7f9-....sentinel
/tmp/intent/in-session-36315235-....sentinel
```

And the only file that mentions them is the one that writes them:

```
$ grep -rl "sentinel" ~/.claude --include="*.sh"
/Users/matts/.claude/skills/in-session/scripts/release-gate.sh
```

Writer, no reader.

## Root Cause

Both documents are GENERATED -- `AGENTS.md` by `intent agents sync`, `CLAUDE.md` from `lib/templates/llm/_CLAUDE.md` (its own footer says so). Their hook sections describe the standard Intent project shape unconditionally, rather than what this project actually has. Neither file is hand-edited here, and editing them would be overwritten on the next sync, so the drift cannot be fixed from inside this repository.

## Impact

Procedural, not a build breakage, which is why this is medium. The gate's job is to make a session load its coding skills before touching code; without it a session can skip `/in-session` entirely and nothing objects. The cost is that the docs assert the safety net exists, so nobody checks -- and the sentinel ritual running successfully every session is active evidence for a mechanism that is not there.

It is the prose form of the failure this project spends most of its rules preventing: a success path that verified nothing. `usage-rules.md` states the rule for gates -- "make a gate that examines nothing FAIL" -- and this is a gate that does not exist reporting nothing at all.

## Proposed Fix

Owner's call, and the two halves live in different places.

1. **In this repository:** either wire the three hooks in `.claude/settings.json` with scripts under `.claude/scripts/`, or accept their absence -- but if they are absent, the generated docs must stop claiming them.
2. **Upstream in Intent:** the `_CLAUDE.md` template and the `agents sync` generator assert the hook architecture unconditionally. They should describe what the project has, or describe the architecture as available-and-optional rather than as wired. Without this, any fix here is undone by the next `intent agents sync`.

Worth deciding alongside it: `release-gate.sh` should arguably say nothing rather than report "released sentinels" when no gate is installed, since a confident success message for a no-op is the same defect one level down.

## Related

- `intent/wip.md` "Documented but absent" -- where this has been recorded as prose
- 0002, 0003 -- the same class in code: a success path claiming more than it verified

## Resolutions

**FIXED 2026-08-09.** Proposed-fix option 1 was taken in its first form: the hooks are now WIRED, not un-documented. The mechanism turned out to exist fleet-wide -- Laksa and Conflab both carry the full three-hook shape -- and Devbin alone had never run the canonical wiring step. `intent claude upgrade --apply` (the generator, not a hand edit) installed `.claude/settings.json` with all three hooks, the three scripts under `.claude/scripts/`, the chained `.git/hooks/pre-commit` critic gate this project was also missing, `.intent_critic.yml`, and the treeindex ignore file; `.gitignore` was normalised so the canon files are tracked.

The gate was proven in BOTH directions before this was written, because a gate that only ever allows is this issue's defect one level down: with this session's real id (its sentinel exists) `require-in-session.sh` exits 0; with a bogus id it exits 2 -- Claude Code's block code -- naming the expected sentinel. The sentinel writer finally has its reader, in this repo.

**What stays upstream, recorded rather than fixed here:** the `_CLAUDE.md` template and `agents sync` describe the hook architecture unconditionally, so a project that deliberately skips wiring (`--skip-settings` exists for exactly that) still gets docs asserting it. And `release-gate.sh` still reports "released sentinels" even where no gate reads them -- a confident no-op, harmless here now, still the same defect in any unwired project. Both belong to Intent's templates, not this repository.
